Sources: Q1FY27 presentation (17-Jul-2026) and call (17-Jul-2026); Q4FY26 presentation and call (5-May-2026); Annual Reports FY25 and FY26 (consolidated P&L, notes 30-37, 41); Q4FY24 presentation; Screener.in for statements (FY24 row patched to the audited basis, see tools/authoring/POONAWALLA.patch.js). The ₹2,500 cr QIP of 13-Apr-2026 is in FY27E. A further ₹3,000 cr raise in FY28E is our assumption (not announced): see _capitalRaiseWhy.

history._why: aum = company AUM at March (FY23-FY24 Q4FY24 presentation p32, standalone; FY25-FY26 Q4FY26 presentation p20). provisions = company 'credit cost' = impairment on financial instruments + net loss on derecognition of financial instruments (loss on sale of NPAs to ARCs): FY26 ₹1,104.13 + ₹105.79 cr; FY25 ₹1,458.17 + ₹94.41 cr (incl. the ₹666 cr one-time accelerated provision on the discontinued short-ticket personal-loan book in Q2FY25); FY24 ₹72.02 cr (before the ₹1,473 cr exceptional provision and write-off on the legacy Magma book, which sits in exceptional items with the ₹2,309 cr gain on the housing sale). feeIncome = revenue from operations less interest income (fees and commission incl. cross-sell, servicing income, net gain on derecognition/assignment, rental and fair-value gains). Each ties to the audited consolidated P&L; FY26 ties to Screener (revenue ₹6,790 cr; expenses ₹3,210 cr = opex excl. depreciation ₹2,001 cr + provisions ₹1,210 cr).

assumptions._aumGrowthWhy: Guidance: AUM growth of ~35-40% CAGR 'over the next couple of years' (Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 presentations p6); Q1FY27 grew 11.1% QoQ and 62.5% YoY to ₹67,054 cr. We take the top of the range for FY27 (needs ~8% a quarter for Q2-Q4, below Q1's 11%), then fade to 32% and 27% as the book passes ₹1 lakh cr and capital binds (the MD said the April QIP covers 'the next 4 to 5 quarters').
assumptions._yieldOnAumWhy: Interest income ÷ average AUM: 13.4% FY24, 12.8% FY25, 12.8% FY26, 13.3% annualised in Q1FY27 (₹2,118 cr). Disbursement yields rose ~40bp in Q4FY26 and ~50bp in Q1FY27 on mix (Prime PL, gold, consumer durables, CV). We add ~15bp in FY27 and ~10bp in FY28, then hold: secured LAP (28% of AUM at 9.75-12%) and education loans (10.5-13%) cap the blend.
assumptions._feeIncomePctWhy: Fees and other operating income ÷ average AUM: 0.97% FY24, 1.03% FY25, 1.35% FY26, 1.37% in Q1FY27 (cross-sell ₹91 cr, servicing ₹70 cr, assignment gains ₹51 cr). Assignment (DA) gains are lumpy (JM Financial called the Q4FY26 level unsustainable); cross-sell grows slower than the book.
assumptions._costOfFundsWhy: Interest expense ÷ average Screener borrowings (incl. lease liabilities): 7.4% FY25, 7.4% FY26, 7.5% annualised in Q1FY27. Company cost of borrowing 7.63% (Q4FY26) and 7.72% (Q1FY27); management expects 'a small uptick here and there' (CFO, 17-Jul-2026). AAA rating (CRISIL, CARE) and NCDs at ~32% of borrowings.
assumptions._opexPctWhy: Operating expenses incl. depreciation ÷ average AUM: 4.3% FY25, 4.4% FY26, 3.96% annualised in Q1FY27 (company basis 4.06%). Management's internal benchmark is a lower ratio each March, with 10-25bp quarterly swings from ~400 new gold branches in FY27. We keep FY27 at the Q1 level (branch build-out absorbs the operating leverage) and take ~15-20bp off a year after that.
assumptions._creditCostWhy: Provisions ÷ average AUM: 4.4% FY25 (incl. the ₹666 cr STPL clean-up), 2.5% FY26, 2.34% annualised in Q1FY27 (company basis 2.40%, from 2.51% in Q4FY26 and 2.62% in Q3FY26). Early delinquency (6-MoB 30+) fell to 0.64% for the Oct-Dec 2025 cohort; write-offs run at ~₹275-280 cr a quarter. Management expects 'structural' improvement for 'a couple of quarters' but gives no number. We take ~10bp off Q1 for FY27 and stop at ~2.05%: 46-47% of AUM is unsecured and most of the new books are less than two years old. Brokers: Motilal 2.2%/1.9%, HDFC Securities ~2%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: No dividend for FY25 (loss) or FY26 ('to conserve capital', Annual Report FY26); ₹2 a share was paid for FY24. We assume none for FY27E and a 10% payout from FY28E (Motilal Oswal models 10-11%).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-operating other income: ₹5.47 cr in FY26, ₹7 cr in Q1FY27.
assumptions._capitalRaiseWhy: FY27E: the QIP of 13-Apr-2026 (6.743 cr shares at ₹370.75 = ₹2,500 cr gross). ₹2,454 cr is the equity added in Q1FY27 other than profit (net worth ₹13,060 cr at Jun-26 less ₹10,298 cr at Mar-26 less Q1 PAT ₹308 cr; standalone presentation), i.e. net of issue costs. FY28E: ₹3,000 cr is OUR assumption, not announced. Without it, AUM ÷ net worth reaches ~7x by FY28E and capital adequacy (19.46% in Jun-26, regulatory minimum 15%) would fall below ~15%. The board took a 12-month enabling approval for ₹5,500 cr in Jan-2026, of which ₹2,500 cr was used; the MD said in Jul-2026 that the QIP covers 'the next 4 to 5 quarters'. Emkay also builds in a ₹3,000 cr raise in FY28E. Priced at the 30-Sep-2026 close (₹443.85).

valuation._why: Ke = 6.5% + 1.25 × 6% = 14.0% (house rf and ERP; beta 1.25, above Chola and Shriram at 1.15 and Bajaj Finance at 1.1: ~46% unsecured book, most new products under two years old, a credit event in FY25 and a short record under the current team). sustainableRoe 15% = what a 2.5% ROA on AUM at ~6x AUM ÷ equity gives; our FY29E is ~13%, management's 3-3.5% ROA target would give 17-20%. g = 10% long-run book growth in the justified P/B. Residual income fades ROE to 15% over 8 years with payout rising to 35% (steady-state book growth = 15% × 65% ≈ 10%, consistent with g), 6% terminal growth.

methods.name: P/B
methods.why: The street's method (Motilal Oswal 3.0x and Deven Choksey 3.2x FY28E book; JM Financial 2.2x; Emkay 1.9x). 2.4x = own median one-year-forward P/B since Apr-2021 excluding the dates whose forward year was a trough (FY25 loss, FY26 below half the prior peak EPS) (2.5x; 2.8x on all dates) × the listed-lender P/B move vs five-year medians, Poonawalla excluded (−2.5%) × growth/returns regime 1.00 (the window priced 32-55% AUM growth and 11-14% ROE, as we forecast). Bull 2.8x = median on all dates since 2021; bear 1.9x = the low since the reset (Jun-2026) and the bears' multiple.

methods.name: Justified P/B
methods.why: (ROE − g) ÷ (Ke − g) on book at the 12-month target date.

methods.name: Residual income
methods.why: Book plus the present value of profit above the cost of equity, rolled forward 6 months.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check only. 20x = median forward P/E since Apr-2021 on EPS before one-offs, trough year FY26 left out (25.1x; 21.2x on reported EPS, which carries the FY23-24 exceptional gains) × listed-lender P/E move vs five-year medians (−19.5%) × regime 1.00. Bull 25x = the one-off-adjusted median; bear 18x = the low since the reset (17.7x, Jun-2026).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Management delivers its plan: AUM +43/35/30% (top of guidance and then some), disbursement yields keep rising (+20bp), AI and branch productivity take another 15bp off opex, credit cost falls to ~1.8-1.95% as the new books season well; ROA reaches ~2.7% by FY29E (still short of the 3-3.5% target); long-run ROE 18%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: A second credit event: unseasoned unsecured books (instant loans, Prime PL, business loans) sour as they age, credit cost back near 3% (FY25 was 4.4% incl. one-offs), growth cut to +30/22/17%, funding 20bp dearer and yields 20bp lower as the company retreats to safer loans; long-run ROE 12%.

cover.headline: The clean-up worked and the rebuild is growing fast; the price already assumes management hits a return target it has not yet come close to
cover.lead: Poonawalla Fincorp (the former Magma Fincorp, controlled by the Poonawalla family since 2021) is a ₹67,000 cr consumer and small-business lender. After a FY25 loss from a blown-up short-ticket personal-loan book, a new HDFC Bank-trained team launched six products and grew AUM 62.5% in a year; credit cost fell from ~3.1% to 2.40% and ROA rose from 0.68% to 1.98% in four quarters (Q1FY27). The street values the stock on **P/B (1.9-3.2x FY28E book)**. We forecast EPS of ₹15.3 / ₹22.1 / ₹29.3 for FY27-29E and ROE of {{F.roe.0|pct0}}-{{F.roe.2|pct0}}. Applying **2.4x to Sep-28E book of ₹215** (its own forward P/B median of 2.5x since 2021 with the FY25-26 trough left out, adjusted for the sector) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY**, a fragile one. Our intrinsic cross-checks (justified P/B ₹227, residual income ₹196) are less than half the price, which implies a ~{{dcf.impliedRoe|pct0}} ROE for ever; and the BUY needs a FY28E equity raise at a premium to book (without it ₹470, a HOLD). Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The clean-up worked, and the new engines are running
arguments.p: The erstwhile short-ticket personal-loan book fell from 21% of loans (Sep-2024) to 8% (Mar-2025) after a ₹666 cr accelerated provision. Six-month delinquency on new loans fell from 6.74% (Apr-Jun 2024 cohort) to 0.64% (Oct-Dec 2025). New products (Prime PL, gold, consumer durables, CV, education) were 26% of Q1FY27 disbursements; AUM grew 62.5% to ₹67,054 cr; PAT rose from ₹63 cr to ₹308 cr a quarter in a year.

arguments.h: But growth is not yet profitable growth
arguments.p: FY26 ROE was ~6%. Even on our improving forecast ROE is {{F.roe.0|pct}} / {{F.roe.1|pct}} / {{F.roe.2|pct}} in FY27-29E, below our 14.0% cost of equity. 47% of AUM is unsecured, most new books are under two years old, and growth eats capital: ₹4,000 cr raised from the promoter and a QIP in seven months, and we pencil in another ₹3,000 cr in FY28E.

arguments.h: Targets are ambitious and have moved before
arguments.p: The previous team guided a 4-4.5% ROA in Apr-2024 and delivered a loss. The current MD's 3-3.5% ROA target was "3 years from the day I joined" (Jun-2024) in Apr-2025 and a "June exit of 2028" in Jul-2026. We get to ~{{F.roaAum.2|pct}} by FY29E; brokers to 2.1-2.4% in FY28E. Reaching 3% needs credit cost near 1.5%, a level this book has not shown.

arguments.h: Valuation: fair on the street's yardstick, rich on fundamentals
arguments.p: At ₹444 the stock trades at 3.5x Mar-26 book but 2.2x our FY28E book, below its 2.5x ex-trough median. 2.4x Sep-28E book gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}. On returns it is expensive: residual income at our ROE path is ₹196; the price needs a ~{{dcf.impliedRoe|pct0}} long-run ROE, roughly management's target sustained for ever.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether credit cost keeps falling from 2.40% while ~400 gold branches are added and opex absorbs them.
The next equity raise: the board's 12-month enabling approval (Jan-2026) was for ₹5,500 cr, of which ₹2,500 cr was used; size and price will set the dilution and the book per share.
Seasoning of the new books (Prime PL, consumer durables, CV, gold, education) as they pass 12-24 months on book: early delinquency and Stage 2/3 by product.
ROA progress against the 3-3.5% target (June-2028 exit): we model ~2.1-2.2% in FY28-29E.
Regulation: RBI's draft on revolving credit (6-Aug-2026) and IRDAI's consultation on loan-linked insurance commissions (23-Sep-2026), which touches cross-sell income (₹91 cr in Q1FY27).

sections.title: A consumer and small-business lender rebuilt around thirteen products, half of them secured

blocks.p: Poonawalla Fincorp is a non-deposit-taking NBFC (a lender regulated by the RBI that cannot take public deposits). It lends to salaried and self-employed individuals and small businesses, and to mid-sized companies and other NBFCs. Like every lender it earns the gap between what it charges and what it pays: in FY26 interest income was 12.8% of average AUM, borrowing cost ~7.4-7.7%, operating costs 4.4% and loan losses 2.5%. Of FY26 revenue of ₹6,790 cr, ₹6,141 cr was interest and ₹649 cr fees and other income (fees and commission incl. insurance cross-sell ₹420 cr, gains on selling loans ₹217 cr).

The book has two halves. **Secured** loans (53% in Jun-2026): loans against property (28% of AUM, the largest product), pre-owned car loans, gold loans, used commercial vehicles and machinery and medical equipment. **Unsecured** loans (47%): "instant" digital consumer loans sold through fintech partners (19%, at 22-29% interest), personal loans to employees of large companies ("Prime PL"), business and professional loans and consumer-durable EMI loans. Mid-market loans to rated companies and NBFCs (15%) and education loans for students abroad (2%) complete it. At Mar-2026 the company had 5,860 employees, 500+ branches (400 of them gold-loan branches; 460 by Jul-2026), 2,700+ channel partners and 50+ digital partners.

blocks.callout: **Why this matters:** Poonawalla is no longer a lender whose growth hangs on one product: in FY25 its fastest-growing book, digital small-ticket personal loans (21% of loans in Sep-2024), blew up. Management calls it "6 growth engines mounted on a single chassis", each tied to a different borrower and economic driver. That is a real improvement in diversification. But two things have not changed: almost half the book is unsecured, and most of it is young. Products launched in 2024-25 have not yet been through a full credit cycle, so today's low delinquencies are partly a function of age.

blocks.callout: **The lesson from history:** the stock has twice been priced for returns the business did not then earn: in 2023-24 on write-back-flattered profits and a 4-4.5% ROA guide, and again today on a 3-3.5% target. The FY25 blow-up happened in a product (digital small-ticket loans) that was growing fastest. The new team deserves credit for the clean-up; it has not yet shown a full cycle.

sections.title: Retail lending: a 16%-a-year market in which Poonawalla grows four times as fast

blocks.p: Retail loans across Indian lenders grew more than 16% in the year to Mar-2026, led by gold loans, unsecured personal loans and consumer-durable finance (Poonawalla's chief credit officer, Q1FY27 call). That followed a stress cycle in 2024-25 in small-ticket personal loans, microfinance and small-business loans, which is what hit Poonawalla's STPL book. Poonawalla's AUM grew 69% in FY26 and 62.5% in the year to Jun-2026, about four times the market: this is share-taking through new products and distribution, not a ride on the tide. Every product it sells is contested by banks (which fund themselves more cheaply with deposits), by larger NBFCs (Bajaj Finance, Shriram, Cholamandalam, L&T Finance, Aditya Birla Capital, HDB Financial) and, in personal loans, by fintech platforms that are also its distribution partners.

Among listed retail lenders Poonawalla is mid-sized (market value ₹38,854 cr on 30-Sep-2026, about a fifteenth of Bajaj Finance's) and, on FY26 numbers, the least profitable: an ROE of 5.9% and an ROA of 1.1% against 7-31% and 1.6-6.5% for the others (the low end is Manappuram, hit by its microfinance arm). That gap is the whole investment case: if the rebuild works, returns converge upward; if not, the business stays a fast-growing, low-return lender.

sections.title: Growth: six new engines and a branch roll-out, aiming at 35-40% a year

blocks.p: Disbursements (new loans made) rose from ₹30,240 cr in FY25, a year spent cleaning up, to ₹49,440 cr in FY26. In Q1FY27 the monthly run-rate was ~₹537 cr in Prime PL, ~₹292 cr in gold, ~₹144 cr each in education and consumer durables and ~₹97 cr in CV; new products made up 26% of disbursements against 20% two quarters earlier. AUM grew 10-16% a quarter through FY26 and 11.1% in Q1FY27. Management guides ~35-40% a year "over the next couple of years" and speaks of an "aspiration for 5-6x AUM over the next 5 years" (a ~40% CAGR).

blocks.p: Credit cost (provisions plus losses on selling bad loans) was 5.1% of average AUM in FY25, incl. the ₹666 cr STPL clean-up, and 2.5% in FY26. Write-offs run at ₹275-280 cr a quarter (~1.7% of AUM a year), which management says is now "natural policy" write-off with the legacy book "behind us".

sections.title: Funding: AAA-rated and lengthened, but with no deposit franchise the cost stays ~7.7%

blocks.p: Poonawalla borrows from banks (term loans and working-capital lines), the bond market (NCDs), commercial paper and foreign lenders (ECB). In FY26 it raised ₹13,830 cr through NCDs, lifting them from ~7% of borrowings (Mar-2025) to ~32% (Mar-2026), and long-term money from 75.2% of borrowings (Q1FY26) to 88.5% (Q1FY27). Borrowings were ₹49,866 cr in Jun-2026. CRISIL and CARE rate it AAA/Stable (A1+ for CP), backed by the Poonawalla group; in Dec-2020, before the takeover, Magma was rated AA- (CARE). The cost of borrowing was 7.72% in Q1FY27, down from 8.07% in Q4FY25 but up 9bp on the quarter.

sections.title: Capital: ₹4,000 cr raised in seven months, and the growth plan needs more

blocks.p: Capital adequacy (CRAR) was 19.46% in Jun-2026 (Tier 1 18.37%) against a 15% minimum. It had fallen from 33.8% (Mar-2024) to 22.9% (Mar-2025) and 16.8% (Mar-2026) as the book doubled, and was rebuilt by two raises: ₹1,500 cr from the promoter at ₹452.51 (Sep-2025) and a ₹2,500 cr QIP at ₹370.75 (Apr-2026), 6.74 cr shares or ~8% dilution. Risk weights are ~100-125% on most of the book, so CRAR moves roughly with equity ÷ AUM (19.5% in Jun-2026).

The arithmetic is simple. At ~12-14% ROE and no dividend, retained profit grows equity ~12-15% a year; at 30-40% AUM growth, equity ÷ AUM falls ~3pp a year. Without new money, our model takes it to 14.3% by FY28E, below the regulatory floor once deductions are counted. The MD said in July the QIP leaves the company "comfortable for the next 4 to 5 quarters", and the board's enabling approval of Jan-2026 was for ₹5,500 cr. **We therefore assume a further ₹3,000 cr raise in FY28E** at the 30-Sep close (₹444, 6.8 cr shares, ~7.7% dilution), as Emkay also does. It is not announced.

sections.title: From ROA to ROE: ~2% on assets at ~6x leverage gives only ~12-14%

blocks.p: A lender's return on equity is its return on assets times leverage. Poonawalla earns a high yield, but pays a lot to run its book (opex ~4% of AUM) and loses ~2-2.5% to bad loans, so only ~2% of AUM reaches the bottom line even in our improving forecast. With ~6x AUM ÷ equity, that gives a 12-14% ROE. To reach the 18-20%+ that the share price implies, it needs management's 3-3.5% ROA, or much more leverage, which capital rules do not allow.

sections.title: Five years, three different companies: Magma, a flattered FY24, a FY25 loss, and now a rebuild

blocks.p: Read Poonawalla's history in three acts. **FY21-FY23**: Magma Fincorp is recapitalised by the Poonawalla group (₹3,456 cr in 2021) and cleans up; profit is small. **FY24**: reported profit of ₹1,683 cr and an ROE of 22% look superb, but they are flattered twice: by a ₹2,309 cr gain on selling the housing arm (partly used to provide ₹1,473 cr against the old Magma book) and by provision write-backs that put credit cost near zero (₹72 cr on a ₹25,000 cr book). Before exceptional items FY24 profit was ₹1,045 cr and ROE ~14%. **FY25**: the short-ticket personal-loan book blows up, a ₹666 cr accelerated provision follows, and the year ends in a ₹98 cr loss. **FY26**: a new team grows AUM 69% and profit recovers to ₹542 cr, an ROE of only ~6%.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: strong backing and a deep bench, but no moat yet

blocks.p: A lender's moat shows up as a lasting gap between what it earns on loans and what it pays for funds, costs and losses. Poonawalla has not yet shown one: its ROA was ~1.1% in FY26 against 2-6% for the better listed NBFCs, and its best year (FY24) was flattered by one-offs. We test where an edge could come from.

MD and business heads hired from HDFC Bank, Bandhan, Aditya Birla Finance and others, "2 levels deep" in each new business.
A real asset, but this team has run Poonawalla for only two years and one up-cycle.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but thin provisions and loan-sale gains flatter the trend

blocks.p: We rate accounting **AMBER**. The joint auditors (M S K A & Associates and Kirtane & Pandit) flagged expected credit loss and IT controls as key audit matters; we found no qualification, and disclosure has improved (stage-wise coverage, early-delinquency curves). But a reader should weigh four things:

bullets: **Falling provision cover.** Expected-credit-loss provisions were ₹838.90 cr on ₹56,790 cr of gross loans at Mar-2026 (1.48%) against ~2.8% a year earlier; the auditors note that ECL on new products is set from external bureau data because the company has no history of its own. Lower cover means lower reported credit cost today and less buffer tomorrow.

**Gains on selling loans.** Net gains on derecognition (assignment of loans to banks) were ₹217 cr in FY26, 30% of pre-tax profit, and swing quarter to quarter (₹63 cr, ₹41 cr, ₹78 cr, ₹51 cr in recent quarters). Losses on selling bad loans to ARCs (₹106 cr) are in credit cost, as the company reports it.

**History of one-offs in both directions.** FY23-FY24 profits were lifted by provision write-backs on the Magma book (credit cost −₹134 cr and ₹72 cr); FY24's housing-sale gain was netted against ₹1,473 cr of legacy provisions and write-offs in one exceptional line; FY25 carried the ₹666 cr STPL clean-up. The trend in reported profit since FY23 says little about underlying earning power.

**Write-offs are high relative to NPAs.** ₹975 cr written off (net of recoveries) in FY26, ~2.0% of average AUM, against gross NPA of only ₹818 cr at year-end: low NPA ratios partly reflect fast write-off, so credit cost is the better guide than GNPA.

sections.title: Management and governance: a strong sponsor and an HDFC-trained team, with a short record and a 2021 scare

blocks.p: Adar Poonawalla (CEO of Serum Institute of India) chairs the board as a non-executive promoter director. sections.title: Our honest summary: a BUY on the street's yardstick, with the fundamentals well behind the price

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a promoter-backed, AAA-funded consumer and small-business lender that cleaned up a bad book in FY25, rebuilt itself around thirteen products under an experienced team, and has since tripled its quarterly ROA (0.68% → 1.98%) while growing AUM ~60% a year. **What you are paying:** 3.47x Mar-26 book and 2.2x our FY28E book, for an ROE of ~6% in FY26 and {{F.roe.0|pct0}}-{{F.roe.2|pct0}} in our FY27-29E, below a 14.0% cost of equity. On returns it is expensive: justified P/B ₹227, residual income ₹196, and the price implies a ~{{dcf.impliedRoe|pct0}} ROE for ever. assumptions._note: Poonawalla Fincorp (consolidated = standalone in substance since the housing unit was sold in Jul-2023) lender model, as of 30-Sep-2026 on a Q1FY27 basis. Sources: Q1FY27 presentation (17-Jul-2026) and call (17-Jul-2026); Q4FY26 presentation and call (5-May-2026); Annual Reports FY25 and FY26 (consolidated P&L, notes 30-37, 41); Q4FY24 presentation; Screener.in for statements (FY24 row patched to the audited basis, see tools/authoring/POONAWALLA.patch.js). The ₹2,500 cr QIP of 13-Apr-2026 is in FY27E. A further ₹3,000 cr raise in FY28E is our assumption (not announced): see _capitalRaiseWhy.

history._why: aum = company AUM at March (FY23-FY24 Q4FY24 presentation p32, standalone; FY25-FY26 Q4FY26 presentation p20). provisions = company 'credit cost' = impairment on financial instruments + net loss on derecognition of financial instruments (loss on sale of NPAs to ARCs): FY26 ₹1,104.13 + ₹105.79 cr; FY25 ₹1,458.17 + ₹94.41 cr (incl. the ₹666 cr one-time accelerated provision on the discontinued short-ticket personal-loan book in Q2FY25); FY24 ₹72.02 cr (before the ₹1,473 cr exceptional provision and write-off on the legacy Magma book, which sits in exceptional items with the ₹2,309 cr gain on the housing sale). feeIncome = revenue from operations less interest income (fees and commission incl. cross-sell, servicing income, net gain on derecognition/assignment, rental and fair-value gains). Each ties to the audited consolidated P&L; FY26 ties to Screener (revenue ₹6,790 cr; expenses ₹3,210 cr = opex excl. depreciation ₹2,001 cr + provisions ₹1,210 cr).

base._why: Equity share capital ₹161.59 cr at 31-Mar-2026 at ₹2 face value (Annual Report FY26 consolidated balance sheet) = 80.795 cr shares. Screener's FY26 profit ÷ EPS gives 81.2 cr; the reported weighted average was 79.19 cr (basic EPS ₹6.84) because the 3.31 cr promoter shares were allotted only on 17-Sep-2025.

assumptions._aumGrowthWhy: Guidance: AUM growth of ~35-40% CAGR 'over the next couple of years' (Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 presentations p6); Q1FY27 grew 11.1% QoQ and 62.5% YoY to ₹67,054 cr. We take the top of the range for FY27 (needs ~8% a quarter for Q2-Q4, below Q1's 11%), then fade to 32% and 27% as the book passes ₹1 lakh cr and capital binds (the MD said the April QIP covers 'the next 4 to 5 quarters').
assumptions._yieldOnAumWhy: Interest income ÷ average AUM: 13.4% FY24, 12.8% FY25, 12.8% FY26, 13.3% annualised in Q1FY27 (₹2,118 cr). Disbursement yields rose ~40bp in Q4FY26 and ~50bp in Q1FY27 on mix (Prime PL, gold, consumer durables, CV). We add ~15bp in FY27 and ~10bp in FY28, then hold: secured LAP (28% of AUM at 9.75-12%) and education loans (10.5-13%) cap the blend.
assumptions._feeIncomePctWhy: Fees and other operating income ÷ average AUM: 0.97% FY24, 1.03% FY25, 1.35% FY26, 1.37% in Q1FY27 (cross-sell ₹91 cr, servicing ₹70 cr, assignment gains ₹51 cr). Assignment (DA) gains are lumpy (JM Financial called the Q4FY26 level unsustainable); cross-sell grows slower than the book.
assumptions._costOfFundsWhy: Interest expense ÷ average Screener borrowings (incl. lease liabilities): 7.4% FY25, 7.4% FY26, 7.5% annualised in Q1FY27. Company cost of borrowing 7.63% (Q4FY26) and 7.72% (Q1FY27); management expects 'a small uptick here and there' (CFO, 17-Jul-2026). AAA rating (CRISIL, CARE) and NCDs at ~32% of borrowings.
assumptions._opexPctWhy: Operating expenses incl. depreciation ÷ average AUM: 4.3% FY25, 4.4% FY26, 3.96% annualised in Q1FY27 (company basis 4.06%). Management's internal benchmark is a lower ratio each March, with 10-25bp quarterly swings from ~400 new gold branches in FY27. We keep FY27 at the Q1 level (branch build-out absorbs the operating leverage) and take ~15-20bp off a year after that.
assumptions._creditCostWhy: Provisions ÷ average AUM: 4.4% FY25 (incl. the ₹666 cr STPL clean-up), 2.5% FY26, 2.34% annualised in Q1FY27 (company basis 2.40%, from 2.51% in Q4FY26 and 2.62% in Q3FY26). Early delinquency (6-MoB 30+) fell to 0.64% for the Oct-Dec 2025 cohort; write-offs run at ~₹275-280 cr a quarter. Management expects 'structural' improvement for 'a couple of quarters' but gives no number. We take ~10bp off Q1 for FY27 and stop at ~2.05%: 46-47% of AUM is unsecured and most of the new books are less than two years old. Brokers: Motilal 2.2%/1.9%, HDFC Securities ~2%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: No dividend for FY25 (loss) or FY26 ('to conserve capital', Annual Report FY26); ₹2 a share was paid for FY24. We assume none for FY27E and a 10% payout from FY28E (Motilal Oswal models 10-11%).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-operating other income: ₹5.47 cr in FY26, ₹7 cr in Q1FY27.
assumptions._capitalRaiseWhy: FY27E: the QIP of 13-Apr-2026 (6.743 cr shares at ₹370.75 = ₹2,500 cr gross). ₹2,454 cr is the equity added in Q1FY27 other than profit (net worth ₹13,060 cr at Jun-26 less ₹10,298 cr at Mar-26 less Q1 PAT ₹308 cr; standalone presentation), i.e. net of issue costs. FY28E: ₹3,000 cr is OUR assumption, not announced. Without it, AUM ÷ net worth reaches ~7x by FY28E and capital adequacy (19.46% in Jun-26, regulatory minimum 15%) would fall below ~15%. The board took a 12-month enabling approval for ₹5,500 cr in Jan-2026, of which ₹2,500 cr was used; the MD said in Jul-2026 that the QIP covers 'the next 4 to 5 quarters'. Emkay also builds in a ₹3,000 cr raise in FY28E. Priced at the 30-Sep-2026 close (₹443.85).

valuation._why: Ke = 6.5% + 1.25 × 6% = 14.0% (house rf and ERP; beta 1.25, above Chola and Shriram at 1.15 and Bajaj Finance at 1.1: ~46% unsecured book, most new products under two years old, a credit event in FY25 and a short record under the current team). sustainableRoe 15% = what a 2.5% ROA on AUM at ~6x AUM ÷ equity gives; our FY29E is ~13%, management's 3-3.5% ROA target would give 17-20%. g = 10% long-run book growth in the justified P/B. Residual income fades ROE to 15% over 8 years with payout rising to 35% (steady-state book growth = 15% × 65% ≈ 10%, consistent with g), 6% terminal growth.

methods.name: P/B
methods.why: The street's method (Motilal Oswal 3.0x and Deven Choksey 3.2x FY28E book; JM Financial 2.2x; Emkay 1.9x). 2.4x = own median one-year-forward P/B since Apr-2021 excluding the dates whose forward year was a trough (FY25 loss, FY26 below half the prior peak EPS) (2.5x; 2.8x on all dates) × the listed-lender P/B move vs five-year medians, Poonawalla excluded (−2.5%) × growth/returns regime 1.00 (the window priced 32-55% AUM growth and 11-14% ROE, as we forecast). Bull 2.8x = median on all dates since 2021; bear 1.9x = the low since the reset (Jun-2026) and the bears' multiple.

methods.name: Justified P/B
methods.why: (ROE − g) ÷ (Ke − g) on book at the 12-month target date.

methods.name: Residual income
methods.why: Book plus the present value of profit above the cost of equity, rolled forward 6 months.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check only. 20x = median forward P/E since Apr-2021 on EPS before one-offs, trough year FY26 left out (25.1x; 21.2x on reported EPS, which carries the FY23-24 exceptional gains) × listed-lender P/E move vs five-year medians (−19.5%) × regime 1.00. Bull 25x = the one-off-adjusted median; bear 18x = the low since the reset (17.7x, Jun-2026).
